definitions.explanation: A celestial event where numerous meteors are observed to radiate from a single point in the night sky, caused by the Earth passing through a trail of debris left by a comet.

examples.japanese: {今夜|こんや}は{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}が{見|み}られる。
examples.english: You can see a meteor shower tonight.

examples.japanese: ペルセウス{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}は{毎年|まいとし}{八月|はちがつ}に{見|み}られる。
examples.english: The Perseid meteor shower can be seen every year in August.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}まで{行|い}って、{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}を{観察|かんさつ}するつもりだ。
examples.english: I plan to go up the mountain to observe the meteor shower.

notes:
Composed of {流星|りゅうせい} (meteor, shooting star) + {群|ぐん} (group, swarm). A word that appears frequently in news and conversation, especially during well-known annual meteor shower events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}を{観測|かんそく}する: to observe a meteor shower
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}の{極大|きょくだい}: the peak of a meteor shower
- {流星群|りゅうせいぐん}が{見|み}ごろ: best viewing time for a meteor shower

WELL-KNOWN METEOR SHOWERS IN JAPAN:
- ペルセウス{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Perseid meteor shower (August)
- ふたご{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Geminid meteor shower (December)
- しぶんぎ{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}: Quadrantid meteor shower (January)

RELATED WORDS:
- {流星|りゅうせい}: meteor, shooting star
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}: shooting star — the everyday, poetic term
- {彗星|すいせい}: comet — often the source of meteor shower debris
